fluff.overview: The KR-61 Long-Range Shuttlecraft is the most common aerodyne long-range shuttle in use across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Designed in 2598 to fill the gap between the short-range ST-46 Shuttle and full DropShips, the KR-61 carries small numbers of passengers and modest cargo between planets and jump points whenever an attached DropShip cannot be detached from its JumpShip. Manufactured at facilities across every major faction since its Star League-era introduction, the KR-61 became one of the most widely distributed civilian spacecraft in human space, a common fixture at jump points, orbital stations, and civilian spaceports from the Magistracy of Canopus to the Draconis Combine.
fluff.capabilities:
The KR-61's primary distinction over the shorter-ranged ST-46 is its extended endurance. Carrying double the fuel of that companion design, it can complete round trips to zenith and nadir jump points without refueling stops. A Pitban 300a fusion engine provides propulsion, yielding a safe acceleration of 2G and a maximum of 3G, adequate for civilian in-system transit.

The passenger section includes sleeping, sanitary, and food preparation accommodations for two crew members and two passengers, a level of comfort unusual in small craft of this mass and entirely absent from the ST-46. Six tons of standard armor provides some deterrence against piracy but offers no serious defensive capability, and the KR-61 is entirely unarmed. Its small cargo hold, which also serves as the sole airlock, limits the vessel's utility as a general freighter. These design trade-offs reflect the craft's civilian mandate, prioritizing endurance and crew habitability over payload capacity or combat survivability.
fluff.deployment: The KR-61 serves in virtually every faction across the Inner Sphere and Periphery, operating wherever JumpShips require a dedicated long-range shuttle. It carries passengers, mail, and light cargo consignments between planets and jump points, and is a common sight aboard JumpShips and at orbital facilities throughout known space.
fluff.history:
The ST-46 Shuttle and KR-61 Long-Range Shuttlecraft together form the backbone of civilian small craft logistics across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. The ST-46 entered service first, in 2528, establishing a broad production base among the major Houses as the standard workhorse shuttle for JumpShips, WarShips, space stations, and large transport vessels. The KR-61 followed seventy years later, in 2598, purpose-built to address the ST-46's primary limitation: with only 5 tons of fuel, the ST-46 could not reliably service the long distances between inner system worlds and zenith or nadir jump points. The KR-61's doubled fuel capacity and extended habitability accommodations filled that gap, and the two designs have operated in complementary roles ever since.

Many of the same manufacturing facilities produce both types. Earthwerks Ltd. on Ares maintained uninterrupted Capellan production of both shuttles across every era from the Star League through the ilClan period. Hinsdale Elec on Dover did the same for the Draconis Combine. Andurien AeroTech operated lines for both at Lopez and Westover in Free Worlds League space. The United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora produced both designs for the Outworlds Alliance and later the Raven Alliance. This shared production base helped ensure both types survived the technological regression of the Succession Wars, remaining available across all major factions even as more complex spacecraft fell out of production.

Additional producers served individual factions. Semier Data Tron on Tharkad supplied the Lyran Commonwealth with ST-46s from the Star League through the Civil War era before shutting down during the Jihad. Shipil Company on Skye and Majesty Metals and Manufacturing on Dunianshire each produced the KR-61 without a corresponding ST-46 line. Federated-Boeing Interstellar at Port Simon Shipyards on Galax produced both for the Federated Suns and later the Federated Commonwealth.

Clan versions of both designs emerged centuries into the Succession Wars period. The ST-46C appeared in 2897, initially misidentified by some Inner Sphere observers as captured IS craft given its unarmed civilian configuration. The KR-61C followed in 2851, adopting Clan-grade composite armor for a modest improvement in protection. Full Clan Occupation Zone production of both Clan variants began by 3080, with Clan Jade Falcon's Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten and the Ghost Bear Tseng Facility on Alshain manufacturing both the ST-46C and KR-61C alongside one another, maintaining the paired production pattern established by their Inner Sphere predecessors.
